questions.q: What instructions did Yahweh give Joshua for attacking Ai, including what to do with its spoil?
questions.a: Yahweh told Joshua not to fear, to take all the men of war, go up to Ai, set an ambush behind the city, and do to Ai and its king as he did to Jericho, but they could take its spoil and livestock for themselves.

questions.q: What were the people of Israel allowed to do with the spoil and livestock from Ai, unlike Jericho?
questions.a: Yahweh told the people they could plunder the spoil and livestock of Ai for themselves.

questions.q: How many warriors did Joshua choose and send by night for the ambush of Ai?
questions.a: Joshua chose 30,000 men, warriors of valor, and sent them out by night.

questions.q: What was Joshua’s plan for his main forces when they approached Ai and the men of Ai came out?
questions.a: Joshua planned that he and all the people with him would approach the city, and when the men of Ai came out to meet them as before, they would flee.

questions.q: What were Joshua’s men in ambush to do to the city once they captured it, according to Yahweh’s word?
questions.a: When the men captured the city, they were to burn it with fire, according to the word of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did all the people of Ai and Bethel do when Joshua and his army pretended to be beaten and fled toward the wilderness?
questions.a: All the people in Ai were summoned to pursue Joshua’s army; they pursued Joshua, were drawn away from the city, and left the city open, as did the men of Bethel.

questions.q: What signal did Yahweh tell Joshua to give with his curved sword to initiate the ambush?
questions.a: Yahweh told Joshua to stretch out the curved sword in his hand toward Ai, because he would give it into Joshua’s hand.

questions.q: Who did the men of Israel capture alive from Ai and bring to Joshua?
questions.a: The men of Israel captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

questions.q: How long did Joshua keep his hand stretched out with the curved sword?
questions.a: Joshua did not draw back his hand with which he stretched out the curved sword until he had devoted all the inhabitants of Ai.

questions.q: What did Israel plunder for themselves from Ai, according to Yahweh’s command to Joshua?
questions.a: Israel plundered the livestock and the spoil of Ai for themselves, according to the word of Yahweh which he had commanded Joshua.

questions.q: What did Joshua do with the king of Ai after hanging him on a tree until evening?
questions.a: As the sun was going down, Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree, threw it at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great pile of stones.

commentary.text: The destruction of Ai and its king.
The law read on Ebal and Gerizim.

Verses 1, 2 When we have faithfully put away sin, that accursed thing which separates between us and God, then, and not till then, we may look to hear from God to our comfort; and God's directing us how to go on in our Christian work and warfare, is a good evidence of his being reconciled to us. God encouraged Joshua to proceed. At Ai the spoil was not to be destroyed as at Jericho, therefore there was no danger of the people's committing such a trespass. Achan, who caught at forbidden spoil, lost that, and life, and all; but the rest of the people, who kept themselves from the accursed thing, were quickly rewarded for their obedience. The way to have the comfort of what God allows us, is, to keep from what he forbids us. No man shall lose by self-denial.

Observe Joshua's conduct and prudence. Those that would maintain their spiritual conflicts must not love their ease. Probably he went into the valley alone, to pray to God for a blessing, and he did not seek in vain. He never drew back till the work was done. Those that have stretched out their hands against their spiritual enemies, must never draw them back.

God, the righteous Judge, had sentenced the Canaanites for their wickedness; the Israelites only executed his doom. None of their conduct can be drawn into an example for others. Especial reason no doubt there was for this severity to the king of Ai; it is likely he had been notoriously wicked and vile, and a blasphemer of the God of Israel.

As soon as Joshua got to the mountains Ebal and Gerizim, without delay, and without caring for the unsettled state of Israel, or their enemies, he confirmed the covenant of the Lord with his people, as appointed, De 11; 27. We must not think to defer covenanting with God till we are settled in the world; nor must any business put us from minding and pursuing the one thing needful. The way to prosper is to begin with God, Mt 6:33. They built an altar, and offered sacrifice to God, in token of their dedicating themselves to God, as living sacrifices to his honour, in and by a Mediator. By Christ's sacrifice of himself for us, we have peace with God. It is a great mercy to any people to have the law of God in writing, and it is fit that the written law should be in a known tongue, that it may be seen and read of all men.
